comment: Chromium settings routes Astro's page deliberately does NOT route, and why.
Hand-maintained, and the ONLY hand-maintained input to the settings parity
gate. The denominator it is checked against is measured, not listed:
own router.ts. Every route in it is either claimed by a screen in
src/pages/settings/settings-page.tsx or declared here; the gate
is neither, and fails on an entry here for a route the page DOES route, so a
disposition cannot quietly outlive the reason for it.
google-service   the screen exists to configure a Google service this
browser does not talk to. There is nothing to reimplement.
oxy-replacement  Astro does the same job somewhere else, and that screen is
later-issue-N    it is coming, and issue N owns it.
chromeos-only    the route only exists in a ChromeOS build.
A note is required and is not decoration: it is what tells a later reader
whether the disposition is still true.

ACCOUNT.note: Chrome's Google-account screen. Astro's identity is an Oxy account, and the You and Astro section (/identity) is where it is managed.

AI.note: The container for Chrome's Gemini-backed features. Astro's assistant is Alia, which has its own section; nothing under this route has an Astro equivalent.

AI_TAB_ORGANIZATION.note: Tab organiser, served by Google's model.

COMPARE.note: Product comparison, served by Google's shopping backend.

GEMINI.note: Gemini settings. Astro ships no Gemini integration.

GLIC_SECTION.note: The Gemini launcher's own section. Declared in SettingsRoutes and never constructed in the locked Chromium revision, so upstream itself reaches it in no configuration this build has.

GOOGLE_SERVICES.note: The list of Google services a signed-in profile may enable. Every one of them is removed by the ungoogled patch series.

MANAGE_PROFILE.note: Chrome's profile name, avatar and theme editor. Name and avatar belong to the Oxy account (You and Astro); the theme is Appearance.

OFFER_WRITING_HELP.note: Help me write, served by Google's model.

PEOPLE.note: Chrome's sign-in and sync section. The You and Astro section (/identity) owns identity in Astro, and the fragment is routed there so a bookmark still lands.

PRIVACY_GUIDE.note: A wizard that walks a user through the sync, ad-privacy and safe-browsing choices Astro either removes or decides by default. Walking someone through settings that no longer exist is worse than not offering the walk.

PRIVACY_SANDBOX.note: The Privacy Sandbox ad-targeting APIs. Removed by the ungoogled patch series, so there is no state to show.

PRIVACY_SANDBOX_AD_MEASUREMENT.note: Attribution Reporting. Part of the Privacy Sandbox set above.

PRIVACY_SANDBOX_FLEDGE.note: Protected Audience. Part of the Privacy Sandbox set above.

PRIVACY_SANDBOX_MANAGE_TOPICS.note: Topics API interest editor. Part of the Privacy Sandbox set above.

PRIVACY_SANDBOX_TOPICS.note: Topics API. Part of the Privacy Sandbox set above.

SIGN_OUT.note: Chrome's sign-out dialog. Signing out of an Oxy account happens in You and Astro (/identity).

SYNC.note: Oxy Sync is issue #23. Until it exists there is nothing behind this screen; a stub would imply the browser syncs.

SYNC_ADVANCED.note: The per-data-type controls of the same feature. Issue #23.
